purpose: Identify the minimum semantic information required before the orientation and MTO candidates can be formalized or executed.

orientation_basis.candidate_statement: One symmetry may have multiple admissible orientations.
required_questions: What object or relation is the single symmetry?
What is the complete orientation set?
Are the four orientations exhaustive, minimal, or illustrative?
Is orientation typed independently from position and geometry?
What equivalence relation identifies orientations as aspects of one symmetry?
minimum_acceptance_artifacts: A typed definition of symmetry and orientation.
An explicit finite orientation set or a reason it is not finite.
An admissibility predicate and at least one boundary case.
A falsification condition for the four-orientation claim.

ordinal_traversal.candidate_statement: Ordinal repetition and alternating orientation may generate higher-order structure.
required_questions: What is the index domain and its ordering?
What operation produces the next orientation?
What output is called a trajectory or wave-like projection?
Which properties are invariant under traversal choice?
minimum_acceptance_artifacts: A typed index and traversal rule.
A finite worked example with expected output.
A counterexample or boundary condition for non-alternating sequences.

mto_contract.candidate_statement: Many admissible orientation histories may resolve into one admissible realization.
required_questions: What is the operator name and type signature?
What is its input space: histories, orientations, or typed relations?
What closure condition determines whether an output is admissible?
How is relational history preserved or represented?
Does the operator apply to every admissible input or only a bounded domain?
What failure result applies when closure is unavailable or non-unique?
minimum_acceptance_artifacts: A deterministic finite example with expected result.
A bounded scope statement replacing the unvalidated word universal.
A falsification condition for history preservation.

blocking_conditions: No MTO domain, codomain, closure rule, or failure behavior.
No finite test fixtures or falsification conditions.
No authority for promotion or execution.
next_review_deliverable: A human-approved bounded specification answering the required questions or explicitly rejecting the candidate claims.
